I encountered a strange bug related to verso. The MWE below works fine in VS Code (say, 4.31.0), but lake build Mathlib/VersoBugIncludeDocstring.lean (assume you saved the MWE to this file) yields an error

error: Mathlib/VersoBugIncludeDocstring.lean:38:0: No doc-string for `Nat`

Any ideas how to fix this?

module

public import Lean

open Lean Elab Tactic Doc in
/-- Writing `{insertDocstringOf foo}` inside a verso doc-string inserts the doc-string of
declaration `foo` in the current environment, as a separate paragraph.
If `foo` does not exist or has no doc-string, it throws an error.
-/
@[doc_command] meta def _root_.insertDocstringOf (n : Ident) :
    DocM <| Block ElabInline ElabBlock := do
  let doc ← realizeGlobalConstNoOverloadWithInfo n
  let some docStr ← findDocString? (← getEnv) doc
    | throwError "No doc-string for `{.ofConstName doc}`"
  -- Future: once there is a better auto-converter between markdown and verso doc-strings,
  -- rewrite this code accordingly!
  -- Perhaps, it could be nice to write .verso here.
  return .para #[.text docStr]

/-- `Foo` is my favourite definition -/
def Foo := 0

-- via `lake build`, this works
set_option doc.verso true in
set_option doc.verso.suggestions false in
/-- `bar` is somehow related to `Foo`: let's include its doc-string

{insertDocstringOf Foo}
-/
theorem bar : True := trivial

#check Nat

set_option doc.verso true in
set_option doc.verso.suggestions false in
/-- a doc-string including a doc-string of an item defined in a previous module

{insertDocstringOf Nat}
-/
theorem baz : True := trivial

This is a feature not a bug :upside_down:. It has to do with the different import levels, due to the module system. There are 3 import levels:

  1. import everything from a file
  2. import the public information and the information needed by the language server (this includes doc-strings)
  3. import only the public information (this excludes doc-strings)

You get (1) by writing import all. If you write import without all, you get (2) when opening the file with the lean server, and you get (3) when running the file with lake build.

I think you should be able to work around it by using import all Init.Prelude, so that the doc-string of Nat is also imported.

Thanks for the quick answer. Sadly, it does not work: changing the imports to

public import Lean
import all Init.Prelude -- doc-string for Nat
meta import all Init.Prelude -- doc-string for Nat

in the above (or leaving out the meta line) still yields the same error.

That's right. Modules really have three sets of data, each with its own .olean:

  1. The public part - this is what you get with import. It's the module's interface.
  2. The private part - this is what you get with import all. It's the module's implementation.
  3. The server part - this contains data used for interactive language server work, including the docstrings. These aren't loaded at all in batch mode, and we don't really have a way to do so.

I think a solution to this will have to be similar to the way inherit_docs now works. Instead of copying the docstring, it inserts an indicator that the docstring is inherited into a separate inheritance table that's respected by docstring-lookup functions. For Verso docstrings, we would need a way to insert an indicator that, at docstring-render-time, does the lookup, rather than doing it at elaboration time.

I think this is doable by essentially copying the design from full Verso. There, extensions get to specify how they're to be rendered to HTML or TeX or whatever other format is used. We already have a way to add extensions in the docstring variant, but not a way to write custom Markdown renderers for them. This would be broadly useful for many things.

I see. Thanks for the explanation. So, this needs a Lean core change. How large will it be? Can I hope for this happening soon? (I'd be willing to be mentored, but that would take much longer than e.g. you just implementing this yourself. I'm not familiar with the internals of inherit_doc, for example.)

I'll try to put it together in the next couple of days, this is something that's important to have and I expect you're the first of many users. It's also core enough that I'd rather do it than have help (but thanks for the offer!) and it touches some other work I need to do right now anyway.

I'm not entirely happy with lean4#14115 yet, but I think it does what you want.

Can you take a peek at tests/pkg/verso_doc_md/VersoDocMd/Defs.lean and its sibling test files in that PR and confirm that it's essentially the feature you're looking to implement?

David Thrane Christiansen said:

That's right. Modules really have three sets of data, each with its own .olean:

  1. The public part - this is what you get with import. It's the module's interface.
  2. The private part - this is what you get with import all. It's the module's implementation.
  3. The server part - this contains data used for interactive language server work, including the docstrings. These aren't loaded at all in batch mode, and we don't really have a way to do so.

import all should load both server and private data -- import levels are cumulative. The docstring for Nat is declared in Init.Prleude. Therefore, Michael's import adjustment:

public import Lean
import all Init.Prelude  -- doc-string for Nat

seems like it should work. I am very confused why it does not.
Yes, that's how it ought to work. Fixed in lean4#14120
Oh, wow, nice! I thought the other behavior was intentional, this is wonderful!
@Michael Rothgang : lean4#14115 is now merged, so both approaches will work.
